scope: Source-specific nonclinical publisher access through the existing approved-content contract; no real LifeBridge/Instagram facts or approvals fabricated.
implemented: Existing research-package actor now owns/cache-loads the readonly approved LifeBridge resource; Ask consumes it instead of merely checking whether the UI loader found a file. UI reads through the same actor off the main thread.

Informational queries select one complete relevant approved excerpt per mandatory publisher. Official information is first and authoritative for operational details; founder context remains separately attributed. Output is explicitly partial publisher information, not a medical eligibility assessment or model-generated company facts.

Actual original titles, URLs, retrieved/reviewed timestamps and declared versions are retained. No DOI/publication date is invented from review metadata. Supplied app disclosure and source-discrepancy review notes remain explicitly labeled.

Unrelated or medical queries merely mentioning LifeBridge still use independent scientific retrieval. Publisher material is not inserted into the scientific package, and contextual/sensitive requests do not enter the publisher-only path.

Only local/localhost file resources are accepted, with an8MiB rejection boundary; network URLs are never fetched. Invalid or single-publisher resources remain unavailable. No clipping/truncation or placeholder approved content.

Known exact brand identifiers remain protected through incoming/display translation, including adjacent CJK/Arabic text; this uses existing canonical translation limits/protection rather than a second language setting.

verification.native_scope: Real Qwen Ask generated/reload path plus actual Foundation publisher/engine tests; no official MADLAD verification.

compile_iterations: Initial escaped-string and complex-expression compiler failures executed no tests. Corrected before passing checks; scoring is now a simple one-pass selection.
remaining: Actual founder-approved, licensed current snapshots from both named websites are still absent; do not create an invented LifeBridgeApprovedContent.json. All production organization facts still remain unavailable until the approved resource is provided.

Real source freshness, discrepancy reconciliation and approval/licensing are content-review work. Optional supplied review flags are a presentation mechanism, not automatic semantic conflict detection.
Instagram first-party brand/product content ingestion and brand-only Ask routing remain unfinished separately; the exact account URL/link and identifiers do not satisfy that instruction.
Apple shared-actor loading/presentation, source disclosure/review flags, VoiceOver/RTL/Dynamic Type and navigation remain NOT_RUN.
Official MADLAD query/display inference, language compatibility and native-language/clinical meaning checks remain blocked/unverified. Controlled identifier-runtime tests are not that evidence.

resource_contract.input: Existing snapshot fields id/title/sourceURL/retrievedAt/reviewedAt/version/approvedText, requiring both official and Carrd hosts; optional sourceDiscrepancies contains actual curator-supplied review notes. No automatic web collection or metadata stamping.
resource_contract.approval: Provide actual approved source material and real review/retrieval metadata; validator/fixtures do not prove review or factual accuracy.
